mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC fell in every week of the window (-22.7 to -50.1) in lockstep with TRANSIT (-41.3 to -73.6) and WORKPLACES (-13.9 to -56.3). Because transit and workplace footfall precede retail footfall, RETAIL_REC's 28-day mean keeps falling over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell 32.3 points and WORKPLACES fell 42.4 points across the four weekly means
failure_condition: The 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC ending 2020-05-13 is above its -40.8 mean over the prior 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Enforced work-from-home holds WORKPLACES below -50 percent of baseline. While that threshold is breached, the weekday commuter and office-lunch customer base is absent, so RETAIL_REC cannot stabilise and its next 14-day mean is lower than the preceding one.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean at or below -50 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped 12.9 points in the latest week, from -43.4 to -56.3
failure_condition: In weeks where WORKPLACES stays at or below -50 percent, the following 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC rises above its preceding 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Trip-chaining collapses when TRANSIT sits below -65 and grocery trips turn negative at the same time. The joint condition removes both the journey and the destination for retail visits, so RETAIL_REC declines faster than either series alone would imply.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT at or below -65 and GROCERY_PHARM at or below -15 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM flipped from +8.0 to -22.1 while TRANSIT fell to -73.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the 14 days after a week meeting the joint trigger is not lower than after weeks that do not meet it.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS is the only series that improved in the latest week (-53.1 to -42.6), showing outdoor trips resume before indoor commerce. If parks traffic keeps recovering, retail trips follow within roughly two weeks and lift RETAIL_REC above its prior four-week mean.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean improves by more than 5 points for a second consecutive week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS gained 10.5 points in the latest week while every other series fell
regime_hint: partial reopening with movement limits eased for outdoor activity only
failure_condition: PARKS improves for a second consecutive week but the 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC ending 2020-05-13 stays at or below -40.8.

mechanism_narrative: The prior 28 days contained the Easter long weekend, which inflates holiday shopping and outdoor trips, while the next 28 days contain only Anzac Day. This calendar asymmetry by itself lowers the next-window RETAIL_REC mean even with restrictions unchanged.
evidence_refs: fact:Easter 2020 fell on 10-13 April, inside the prior 28-day window
fact:PARKS moved -26.4, -32.6, -53.1, -42.6 across the window, showing holiday-sensitive outdoor swings
regime_hint: tightening restrictions with an unchanged holiday calendar effect
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 28-day mean ending 2020-05-13 exceeds the -40.8 mean of the prior 28 days despite the holiday-heavy window being the earlier one.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL above +20 percent is the observable marker of stay-at-home compliance. While it holds above that level, discretionary retail trips stay suppressed, so the next weekly mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the latest weekly mean of -50.1.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean stays above +20 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from +10.3 to +24.3 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: In weeks when RESIDENTIAL stays above +20 percent, the following 7-day mean of RETAIL_REC is higher than the latest weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: The gap between rising RESIDENTIAL (+24.3) and falling WORKPLACES (-56.3) measures how completely out-of-home activity has been substituted into the home. A widening gap predicts a deeper retail contraction over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL minus WORKPLACES widens by more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:the RESIDENTIAL-to-WORKPLACES gap widened from 24.2 to 80.6 points across the window
failure_condition: In weeks when the RESIDENTIAL-to-WORKPLACES gap widens by more than 10 points, RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean is not lower than its preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Once GROCERY_PHARM drops below -20 and RESIDENTIAL stops rising, household stockpiling and confinement are jointly exhausted. The marginal trip then shifts back toward mixed retail, raising RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean above the prior one.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM at or below -20 with RESIDENTIAL rising less than 1 point week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL's weekly increase shrank from 8.6 to 2.4 to 3.0 points while GROCERY_PHARM fell to -22.1
regime_hint: plateau phase where restrictions are no longer tightening
failure_condition: After the trigger fires, RETAIL_REC's following 28-day mean remains at or below its preceding 28-day mean.
